body: People applying for an Australian visa in India may now be asked to provide biometrics, meaning fingerprints and a facial image, as part of the application. The Australian High Commission in New Delhi announced the change from 26 October 2026.

The High Commission says India is one of nearly 60 countries where Australia is expanding biometric collection. The rule applies only to new applications lodged from 26 October; applications already submitted are not affected.
This matters for Melbourne families sponsoring or inviting parents, relatives and friends from India, such as for visitor visas.

ul: The Department of Home Affairs tells each applicant whether they need to provide biometrics, with instructions.
Depending on their circumstances, applicants may be asked to attend an Australian Biometrics Collection Centre in person.
Eligible applicants who have given biometrics at a collection centre before and hold a valid passport may be able to use the Australian Immi App instead, at no cost.
The High Commission says visa processing times are not expected to be affected.

body: The announcement does not list which visa types or age groups are covered. Applicants should follow the instructions they receive from Home Affairs.

body: Diwali falls on Sunday 8 November this year, the date set by the lunar calendar. For many Hindu, Sikh and Jain families in Melbourne, the day brings prayers, lamps, sweets and visits to family and friends.

Public celebrations started early. Melbourne Diwali, a free festival run by the not-for-profit SarasCare, was scheduled for Saturday 31 October at Marvel Stadium Square in Docklands, from 2pm to 10pm.

On Saturday 7 November the Immigration Museum on Flinders Street held a day of free Diwali activities, including henna, rangoli and traditional games. In ticketed Indian embroidery workshops, visitors added their own work to a shared 10-metre textile artwork.

Many Hindu temples and Sikh gurdwaras across Melbourne hold special prayers and services around Diwali. For Sikhs, the day is also Bandi Chhor Divas, which marks the release of Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji from imprisonment. Check with your local temple or gurdwara for times.

The next major date for many in the community is the Gurpurab of Guru Nanak Dev Ji later this month. Published calendars list it on 24 or 25 November, depending on the calendar and time zone used, so confirm the dates of nagar kirtans and services with your gurdwara.

body: चंद्र पंचांग के अनुसार इस साल दिवाली रविवार, 8 नवंबर को है। मेलबर्न में बहुत से हिंदू, सिख और जैन परिवारों के लिए यह दिन पूजा, दीयों, मिठाइयों और अपनों से मिलने-जुलने का दिन है।

सार्वजनिक उत्सव पहले ही शुरू हो गए थे। गैर-लाभकारी संस्था SarasCare द्वारा आयोजित निःशुल्क 'मेलबर्न दिवाली' उत्सव शनिवार, 31 अक्टूबर को डॉकलैंड्स के मार्वल स्टेडियम स्क्वेयर में दोपहर 2 बजे से रात 10 बजे तक होना तय था।

शनिवार, 7 नवंबर को फ़्लिंडर्स स्ट्रीट स्थित इमिग्रेशन म्यूज़ियम में दिवाली की निःशुल्क गतिविधियाँ हुईं, जिनमें मेहंदी, रंगोली और पारंपरिक खेल शामिल थे। टिकट वाली भारतीय कढ़ाई कार्यशालाओं में लोगों ने 10 मीटर लंबी साझा कपड़ा-कलाकृति में अपना योगदान जोड़ा।

दिवाली के आसपास मेलबर्न के कई हिंदू मंदिरों और सिख गुरुद्वारों में विशेष पूजा और दीवान होते हैं। सिखों के लिए यह दिन बंदी छोड़ दिवस भी है, जो गुरु हरगोबिंद साहिब जी की क़ैद से रिहाई की याद में मनाया जाता है। समय जानने के लिए अपने नज़दीकी मंदिर या गुरुद्वारे से संपर्क करें।

समुदाय में बहुतों के लिए अगली बड़ी तारीख़ इसी महीने गुरु नानक देव जी का प्रकाश पर्व (गुरपुरब) है। अलग-अलग कैलेंडर और समय-क्षेत्र के हिसाब से प्रकाशित पंचांगों में इसकी तारीख़ 24 या 25 नवंबर दी गई है, इसलिए नगर कीर्तन और दीवानों की तारीख़ अपने गुरुद्वारे से पक्की कर लें।

body: ਚੰਦਰ ਕੈਲੰਡਰ ਮੁਤਾਬਕ ਇਸ ਸਾਲ ਦੀਵਾਲੀ ਐਤਵਾਰ, 8 ਨਵੰਬਰ ਨੂੰ ਹੈ। ਮੈਲਬਰਨ ਦੇ ਬਹੁਤ ਸਾਰੇ ਹਿੰਦੂ, ਸਿੱਖ ਅਤੇ ਜੈਨ ਪਰਿਵਾਰਾਂ ਲਈ ਇਹ ਦਿਨ ਅਰਦਾਸ-ਪੂਜਾ, ਦੀਵਿਆਂ, ਮਠਿਆਈਆਂ ਅਤੇ ਆਪਣਿਆਂ ਨੂੰ ਮਿਲਣ ਦਾ ਦਿਨ ਹੈ।

ਜਨਤਕ ਜਸ਼ਨ ਪਹਿਲਾਂ ਹੀ ਸ਼ੁਰੂ ਹੋ ਗਏ ਸਨ। ਗੈਰ-ਮੁਨਾਫ਼ਾ ਸੰਸਥਾ SarasCare ਵੱਲੋਂ ਕਰਵਾਇਆ ਜਾਂਦਾ ਮੁਫ਼ਤ 'ਮੈਲਬਰਨ ਦੀਵਾਲੀ' ਮੇਲਾ ਸ਼ਨੀਵਾਰ, 31 ਅਕਤੂਬਰ ਨੂੰ ਡੌਕਲੈਂਡਜ਼ ਦੇ ਮਾਰਵਲ ਸਟੇਡੀਅਮ ਸਕੁਏਅਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਦੁਪਹਿਰ 2 ਵਜੇ ਤੋਂ ਰਾਤ 10 ਵਜੇ ਤੱਕ ਹੋਣਾ ਤੈਅ ਸੀ।

ਸ਼ਨੀਵਾਰ, 7 ਨਵੰਬਰ ਨੂੰ ਫ਼ਲਿੰਡਰਜ਼ ਸਟ੍ਰੀਟ ਸਥਿਤ ਇਮੀਗ੍ਰੇਸ਼ਨ ਮਿਊਜ਼ੀਅਮ ਵਿੱਚ ਦੀਵਾਲੀ ਦੀਆਂ ਮੁਫ਼ਤ ਗਤੀਵਿਧੀਆਂ ਹੋਈਆਂ, ਜਿਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਮਹਿੰਦੀ, ਰੰਗੋਲੀ ਅਤੇ ਰਵਾਇਤੀ ਖੇਡਾਂ ਸ਼ਾਮਲ ਸਨ। ਟਿਕਟ ਵਾਲੀਆਂ ਭਾਰਤੀ ਕਢਾਈ ਵਰਕਸ਼ਾਪਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਲੋਕਾਂ ਨੇ 10 ਮੀਟਰ ਲੰਮੀ ਸਾਂਝੀ ਕੱਪੜਾ-ਕਲਾਕ੍ਰਿਤੀ ਵਿੱਚ ਆਪਣਾ ਹਿੱਸਾ ਪਾਇਆ।

ਦੀਵਾਲੀ ਦੇ ਆਸ-ਪਾਸ ਮੈਲਬਰਨ ਦੇ ਕਈ ਹਿੰਦੂ ਮੰਦਰਾਂ ਅਤੇ ਗੁਰਦੁਆਰਿਆਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਖ਼ਾਸ ਪੂਜਾ ਅਤੇ ਦੀਵਾਨ ਸਜਦੇ ਹਨ। ਸਿੱਖਾਂ ਲਈ ਇਹ ਦਿਨ ਬੰਦੀ ਛੋੜ ਦਿਵਸ ਵੀ ਹੈ, ਜੋ ਗੁਰੂ ਹਰਗੋਬਿੰਦ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਜੀ ਦੀ ਕੈਦ ਤੋਂ ਰਿਹਾਈ ਦੀ ਯਾਦ ਵਿੱਚ ਮਨਾਇਆ ਜਾਂਦਾ ਹੈ। ਸਮੇਂ ਲਈ ਆਪਣੇ ਨੇੜਲੇ ਮੰਦਰ ਜਾਂ ਗੁਰਦੁਆਰੇ ਨਾਲ ਸੰਪਰਕ ਕਰੋ।

ਭਾਈਚਾਰੇ ਵਿੱਚ ਬਹੁਤਿਆਂ ਲਈ ਅਗਲੀ ਵੱਡੀ ਤਰੀਕ ਇਸੇ ਮਹੀਨੇ ਗੁਰੂ ਨਾਨਕ ਦੇਵ ਜੀ ਦਾ ਪ੍ਰਕਾਸ਼ ਪੁਰਬ ਹੈ। ਵੱਖ-ਵੱਖ ਕੈਲੰਡਰਾਂ ਅਤੇ ਸਮਾਂ-ਖੇਤਰਾਂ ਮੁਤਾਬਕ ਛਪੀਆਂ ਜੰਤਰੀਆਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਇਸਦੀ ਤਰੀਕ 24 ਜਾਂ 25 ਨਵੰਬਰ ਦਿੱਤੀ ਗਈ ਹੈ, ਇਸ ਲਈ ਨਗਰ ਕੀਰਤਨ ਅਤੇ ਦੀਵਾਨਾਂ ਦੀ ਤਰੀਕ ਆਪਣੇ ਗੁਰਦੁਆਰੇ ਤੋਂ ਪੱਕੀ ਕਰ ਲਓ।

body: When Prime Minister Anthony Albanese hosted Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi for the third Australia–India Annual Summit in Melbourne in July, the two leaders reaffirmed their commitment to a Comprehensive Economic Cooperation Agreement (CECA). Modi said the two countries had decided to "work at a fast pace" on the CECA and on a bilateral investment treaty.

India's Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal and Australia's Trade Minister Don Farrell discussed speeding up the negotiations when they met on the sidelines of the G20 trade ministers' meeting in Milwaukee on 30 September and 1 October, according to a post by Goyal. No timetable for concluding the agreement has been announced, The Indian Sun reported.

The interim Economic Cooperation and Trade Agreement (ECTA) has been in force since 29 December 2022. From 1 January 2026, eligible Indian goods gained duty-free access across all Australian tariff lines, subject to rules of origin.
India was Australia's sixth-largest trading partner in 2025, with two-way trade in goods and services worth A$50.2 billion, according to the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade.

ul: A Joint Declaration on Defence and Security Cooperation, and a new partnership on cyber, critical technologies and supply chains.
An arrangement enabling long-term Australian uranium exports to India, for peaceful purposes only and under international (IAEA) safeguards.
Approval for Melbourne's Victoria University to operate a campus in Gurugram, and a letter of intent for a Flinders University campus in Bengaluru.
$10 million for the Centre for Australia-India Relations' Maitri grants, which support business and people-to-people links.
A temporary space tracking terminal on the Cocos (Keeling) Islands to support India's Gaganyaan human spaceflight program.

body: "Our partnership has never been stronger," Albanese said after the talks. Modi said the relationship was "not just a partnership for the present; it is also a partnership for the future."

body: India has overtaken England as the most common overseas country of birth for people living in Australia, according to Australian Bureau of Statistics figures released on 29 April 2026.

About 971,000 India-born people were living in Australia at 30 June 2025, with the England-born population also at about 971,000. India narrowly overtook England during 2025, the first time it has held the top position.

The India-born population also recorded the largest increase of any birthplace group since 2015, rising by 522,000. The Italy-born and England-born populations recorded the largest decreases over the same period.
Overall, 8.8 million people living in Australia, or 32 per cent of the population, were born overseas.

The milestone was noted in July, when Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi met in Melbourne. Their joint statement said the Indian community in Australia was "now Australia's largest overseas-born group".

body: Indian passport, visa and other consular applications in Australia are now handled through six VFS Global centres, in Adelaide, Brisbane, Canberra, Melbourne, Perth and Sydney, VFS Global said in July.

The Melbourne centre is on the ground floor of 324 St Kilda Road, Melbourne. Applicants book an appointment online through VFS Global's India–Australia portal. Applications are taken Monday to Friday, 8.30am to 4pm, except on public holidays and holidays declared by the Indian mission.
A VFS Global service charge of $115 per application applies from 23 July 2026, in addition to the Government of India fee, SBS Hindi reported, citing an announcement by the High Commission of India.

New passport and visa applications in Australia were suspended from 1 July while a dispute over the tender for India's outsourced consular services went through the Indian courts, Bloomberg reported. The High Commission of India in Canberra announced the restart on 23 July.

In May, SBS Hindi reported that India's Consul General in Melbourne, Anish Rajan, had announced a move from the Swanston Street office to a larger centre on St Kilda Road, with extra counters to shorten booking waits.

body: The federal government has set the 2027 National Planning Level for new international student commencements at 295,000, unchanged from 2026, Study Australia announced in July.

The government says the planning level is not a cap on student numbers. Student visa applications are processed as a priority until a student's chosen provider reaches 80 per cent of its allocation. Applications after that point are still accepted but processed more slowly.
No active provider will receive a lower allocation in 2027 than in 2026, and TAFE students remain exempt from the planning level, The PIE News reported.

The student visa (subclass 500) application fee starts at A$2,500, according to the Department of Home Affairs. A lower fee applies to some applicants, including those enrolling in standalone English language (ELICOS) or non-award courses.
Education Minister Jason Clare said, as reported by The PIE News: "International education is an incredibly important export industry for Australia, but we need to manage it sustainably."

Melbourne's Victoria University received approval in July to open a campus in Gurugram, near Delhi. The university said the campus would teach through its block model, with students studying one subject at a time in four-week blocks, and that it was scheduled to open in August 2026.

body: The City of Melbourne's 2026–27 budget includes more than $1.2 million to keep developing a Little India precinct in Docklands. The council's aim is a recognisable cultural destination alongside Chinatown and Koreatown, built through infrastructure, events and creative projects.

The funding was first flagged in the council's draft budget in March. Councillor Philip Le Liu said at the time, Melbourning reported: "As Australia's most multicultural city, we're taking big steps to make Little India a reality."

In its response to budget consultation, the council said it would focus on "testing future ideas for Little India". It has committed to engaging extensively with Docklands residents and Indian communities, and to running trial experiences so people can try ideas and help shape future plans.
More than 550 people contributed to the council's wider budget consultation, which ran from 31 March to 28 April.
No opening date has been announced. Lord Mayor Nick Reece discussed the project with SBS Hindi in May, and SBS reported that he had invited Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi to an official opening.

Local newspaper Docklands News reported that the council's consultation summary found a minority of submissions supported a Little India in Docklands, while most urged caution about a single-theme precinct. Concerns included top-down delivery and money being diverted from the suburb's other needs, with many residents pointing to greening, shade, wind protection and better public spaces.

The council has kept the $1.2 million commitment but is taking a staged approach that starts with trial activations, the paper reported. Council officers have said no exact location has been chosen, and the council has committed to finalising a Docklands public realm improvements plan.

At a budget hearing on 12 May, Federation of Indian Associations of Victoria president Vasan Srinivasan called the funding a "positive and historic beginning", but said a world-class precinct would need between $5 million and $10 million, Docklands News reported.

The proposal has also drawn what The Australia Today described in April as "negative and, at times, racist commentary". Mr Srinivasan launched a petition in support of the precinct, the outlet reported.
Victoria's strengthened anti-vilification laws, which added new civil protections from 15 April 2026, apply to public conduct online as well as offline.

body.note: We will report consultation dates for Little India as soon as the council announces them.

en.dek: The City of Melbourne has set aside more than $1.2 million to develop a Little India precinct in Docklands, but no site has been chosen and many local residents have urged caution.

body: Community associations, temples, gurdwaras, cultural groups and trader associations can apply for Victorian Government funding, but most rounds open once a year and close within a few weeks. All three of the main 2026 programs below have now closed.

Grants ranged from $5,000 for smaller community events to $50,000 for events of any size, with a further $1 million set aside for events in rural and regional Victoria. Events had to be free, inclusive, accessible and culturally safe. Applications closed on 17 April 2026.

This $5 million program had three streams offering up to $10,000, $100,000 or $400,000 for skills, partnerships and leadership, and for day-to-day costs such as IT systems and business planning. Organisations from new and emerging communities, and from rural and regional areas, were a priority. Applications closed on 19 February 2026.

This fund offered $5,000 grants to not-for-profit business associations, such as trader groups and chambers of commerce, to run advice, training or mentoring for multicultural small business owners and their staff. Each project needed at least 10 participants. Applications closed at 4pm on 28 September 2026, and funded projects must be finished by 26 February 2027.

body: सामुदायिक संघ, मंदिर, गुरुद्वारे, सांस्कृतिक समूह और व्यापारी संघ विक्टोरियाई सरकार से फ़ंडिंग के लिए आवेदन कर सकते हैं, लेकिन ज़्यादातर दौर साल में एक बार खुलते हैं और कुछ ही हफ़्तों में बंद हो जाते हैं। नीचे दिए गए 2026 के तीनों मुख्य कार्यक्रम अब बंद हो चुके हैं।

छोटे सामुदायिक कार्यक्रमों के लिए $5,000 से लेकर किसी भी आकार के कार्यक्रम के लिए $50,000 तक के अनुदान थे, और ग्रामीण व क्षेत्रीय विक्टोरिया के कार्यक्रमों के लिए अलग से $1 मिलियन रखे गए। कार्यक्रमों का निःशुल्क, सबके लिए खुला, सुलभ और सांस्कृतिक रूप से सुरक्षित होना ज़रूरी था। आवेदन 17 अप्रैल 2026 को बंद हुए।

$5 मिलियन के इस कार्यक्रम में तीन श्रेणियाँ थीं, जिनमें कौशल, साझेदारी और नेतृत्व के लिए, और आईटी सिस्टम व व्यावसायिक योजना जैसे रोज़मर्रा के ख़र्चों के लिए $10,000, $100,000 या $400,000 तक मिल सकते थे। नए और उभरते समुदायों तथा ग्रामीण व क्षेत्रीय इलाक़ों के संगठनों को प्राथमिकता दी गई। आवेदन 19 फ़रवरी 2026 को बंद हुए।

इस कोष में गैर-लाभकारी व्यापार संघों, जैसे ट्रेडर समूहों और चैंबर ऑफ़ कॉमर्स, को $5,000 के अनुदान दिए गए, ताकि वे बहुसांस्कृतिक छोटे व्यवसायों के मालिकों और कर्मचारियों के लिए सलाह, प्रशिक्षण या मार्गदर्शन दे सकें। हर परियोजना में कम से कम 10 प्रतिभागी ज़रूरी थे। आवेदन 28 सितंबर 2026 को शाम 4 बजे बंद हुए, और स्वीकृत परियोजनाएँ 26 फ़रवरी 2027 तक पूरी करनी होंगी।

ul: सुनिश्चित करें कि आपके संगठन के पास वैध ABN हो और वह सही नियामक संस्था के पास पंजीकृत हो। व्यवसाय कौशल कोष के लिए दोनों ज़रूरी थे।
अपने संगठन, उसके सदस्यों और पिछले कार्यक्रमों का छोटा विवरण तैयार रखें, जिसे ज़रूरत के हिसाब से बदला जा सके।
साल की शुरुआत से ही विक्टोरियाई सरकार के बहुसांस्कृतिक अनुदान पृष्ठों पर नज़र रखें। 2026 में क्षमता निर्माण और उत्सव वाले दौर जनवरी और मार्च में घोषित हुए थे।

body: ਭਾਈਚਾਰਕ ਸਭਾਵਾਂ, ਮੰਦਰ, ਗੁਰਦੁਆਰੇ, ਸੱਭਿਆਚਾਰਕ ਗਰੁੱਪ ਅਤੇ ਵਪਾਰੀ ਸੰਘ ਵਿਕਟੋਰੀਆ ਸਰਕਾਰ ਤੋਂ ਫ਼ੰਡਿੰਗ ਲਈ ਅਰਜ਼ੀ ਦੇ ਸਕਦੇ ਹਨ, ਪਰ ਬਹੁਤੇ ਗੇੜ ਸਾਲ ਵਿੱਚ ਇੱਕ ਵਾਰ ਖੁੱਲ੍ਹਦੇ ਹਨ ਅਤੇ ਕੁਝ ਹਫ਼ਤਿਆਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਬੰਦ ਹੋ ਜਾਂਦੇ ਹਨ। ਹੇਠਾਂ ਦਿੱਤੇ 2026 ਦੇ ਤਿੰਨੇ ਮੁੱਖ ਪ੍ਰੋਗਰਾਮ ਹੁਣ ਬੰਦ ਹੋ ਚੁੱਕੇ ਹਨ।

ਛੋਟੇ ਭਾਈਚਾਰਕ ਸਮਾਗਮਾਂ ਲਈ $5,000 ਤੋਂ ਲੈ ਕੇ ਕਿਸੇ ਵੀ ਆਕਾਰ ਦੇ ਸਮਾਗਮ ਲਈ $50,000 ਤੱਕ ਦੀਆਂ ਗ੍ਰਾਂਟਾਂ ਸਨ, ਅਤੇ ਪੇਂਡੂ ਤੇ ਖੇਤਰੀ ਵਿਕਟੋਰੀਆ ਦੇ ਸਮਾਗਮਾਂ ਲਈ ਵੱਖਰੇ ਤੌਰ 'ਤੇ $1 ਮਿਲੀਅਨ ਰੱਖੇ ਗਏ। ਸਮਾਗਮਾਂ ਦਾ ਮੁਫ਼ਤ, ਸਾਰਿਆਂ ਲਈ ਖੁੱਲ੍ਹਾ, ਪਹੁੰਚਯੋਗ ਅਤੇ ਸੱਭਿਆਚਾਰਕ ਤੌਰ 'ਤੇ ਸੁਰੱਖਿਅਤ ਹੋਣਾ ਜ਼ਰੂਰੀ ਸੀ। ਅਰਜ਼ੀਆਂ 17 ਅਪ੍ਰੈਲ 2026 ਨੂੰ ਬੰਦ ਹੋਈਆਂ।

$5 ਮਿਲੀਅਨ ਦੇ ਇਸ ਪ੍ਰੋਗਰਾਮ ਵਿੱਚ ਤਿੰਨ ਸ਼੍ਰੇਣੀਆਂ ਸਨ, ਜਿਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਹੁਨਰ, ਭਾਈਵਾਲੀਆਂ ਅਤੇ ਲੀਡਰਸ਼ਿਪ ਲਈ, ਅਤੇ ਆਈਟੀ ਸਿਸਟਮ ਤੇ ਕਾਰੋਬਾਰੀ ਯੋਜਨਾਬੰਦੀ ਵਰਗੇ ਰੋਜ਼ਾਨਾ ਖ਼ਰਚਿਆਂ ਲਈ $10,000, $100,000 ਜਾਂ $400,000 ਤੱਕ ਮਿਲ ਸਕਦੇ ਸਨ। ਨਵੇਂ ਅਤੇ ਉੱਭਰ ਰਹੇ ਭਾਈਚਾਰਿਆਂ ਅਤੇ ਪੇਂਡੂ ਤੇ ਖੇਤਰੀ ਇਲਾਕਿਆਂ ਦੀਆਂ ਸੰਸਥਾਵਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਪਹਿਲ ਦਿੱਤੀ ਗਈ। ਅਰਜ਼ੀਆਂ 19 ਫ਼ਰਵਰੀ 2026 ਨੂੰ ਬੰਦ ਹੋਈਆਂ।

ਇਸ ਫ਼ੰਡ ਵਿੱਚ ਗੈਰ-ਮੁਨਾਫ਼ਾ ਵਪਾਰਕ ਸੰਘਾਂ, ਜਿਵੇਂ ਵਪਾਰੀ ਗਰੁੱਪਾਂ ਅਤੇ ਚੈਂਬਰ ਆਫ਼ ਕਾਮਰਸ, ਨੂੰ $5,000 ਦੀਆਂ ਗ੍ਰਾਂਟਾਂ ਦਿੱਤੀਆਂ ਗਈਆਂ, ਤਾਂ ਜੋ ਉਹ ਬਹੁ-ਸੱਭਿਆਚਾਰਕ ਛੋਟੇ ਕਾਰੋਬਾਰਾਂ ਦੇ ਮਾਲਕਾਂ ਅਤੇ ਮੁਲਾਜ਼ਮਾਂ ਲਈ ਸਲਾਹ, ਸਿਖਲਾਈ ਜਾਂ ਰਹਿਨੁਮਾਈ ਦੇ ਸਕਣ। ਹਰ ਪ੍ਰੋਜੈਕਟ ਵਿੱਚ ਘੱਟੋ-ਘੱਟ 10 ਭਾਗੀਦਾਰ ਜ਼ਰੂਰੀ ਸਨ। ਅਰਜ਼ੀਆਂ 28 ਸਤੰਬਰ 2026 ਨੂੰ ਸ਼ਾਮ 4 ਵਜੇ ਬੰਦ ਹੋਈਆਂ, ਅਤੇ ਮਨਜ਼ੂਰ ਪ੍ਰੋਜੈਕਟ 26 ਫ਼ਰਵਰੀ 2027 ਤੱਕ ਪੂਰੇ ਕਰਨੇ ਹੋਣਗੇ।

ul: ਯਕੀਨੀ ਬਣਾਓ ਕਿ ਤੁਹਾਡੀ ਸੰਸਥਾ ਕੋਲ ਚਾਲੂ ABN ਹੋਵੇ ਅਤੇ ਉਹ ਸਹੀ ਰੈਗੂਲੇਟਰ ਕੋਲ ਰਜਿਸਟਰਡ ਹੋਵੇ। ਕਾਰੋਬਾਰੀ ਹੁਨਰ ਫ਼ੰਡ ਲਈ ਦੋਵੇਂ ਜ਼ਰੂਰੀ ਸਨ।
ਆਪਣੀ ਸੰਸਥਾ, ਇਸਦੇ ਮੈਂਬਰਾਂ ਅਤੇ ਪਿਛਲੇ ਸਮਾਗਮਾਂ ਦਾ ਛੋਟਾ ਵੇਰਵਾ ਤਿਆਰ ਰੱਖੋ, ਜਿਸਨੂੰ ਲੋੜ ਮੁਤਾਬਕ ਬਦਲਿਆ ਜਾ ਸਕੇ।
ਸਾਲ ਦੇ ਸ਼ੁਰੂ ਤੋਂ ਹੀ ਵਿਕਟੋਰੀਆ ਸਰਕਾਰ ਦੇ ਬਹੁ-ਸੱਭਿਆਚਾਰਕ ਗ੍ਰਾਂਟਾਂ ਵਾਲੇ ਪੰਨਿਆਂ 'ਤੇ ਨਜ਼ਰ ਰੱਖੋ। 2026 ਵਿੱਚ ਸਮਰੱਥਾ ਨਿਰਮਾਣ ਅਤੇ ਤਿਉਹਾਰਾਂ ਵਾਲੇ ਗੇੜਾਂ ਦਾ ਐਲਾਨ ਜਨਵਰੀ ਅਤੇ ਮਾਰਚ ਵਿੱਚ ਹੋਇਆ ਸੀ।

body.note: 2027 ਦੇ ਪ੍ਰੋਗਰਾਮਾਂ ਦਾ ਐਲਾਨ ਅਜੇ ਨਹੀਂ ਹੋਇਆ। ਨਿਯਮ ਅਤੇ ਰਕਮਾਂ ਬਦਲ ਸਕਦੀਆਂ ਹਨ।

body: The Department of Home Affairs changed the rules for Student visa (subclass 500) and Student Guardian visa (subclass 590) applications on 2 October 2026. The changes affect where people can apply from and whether family members can be included.

If you already hold a Student visa, the department says the changes do not affect your current visa. Applications lodged before 2 October, including those that listed family members, are assessed under the old rules.

According to the department's factsheet, most temporary visa holders in Australia can no longer lodge a Student or Student Guardian visa application while in Australia. This includes current Student visa holders applying for another Student visa, unless an exemption applies.
Current Student Guardian visa holders can still lodge a further Student Guardian visa application in Australia, the factsheet says.
If the new rules stop you applying onshore, you must be outside Australia both when you lodge the application and when the visa is granted.

body.h: Exemptions for further study in Australia

ul: You need up to 12 more months to finish your course with the same education provider
You are moving to a higher Australian Qualifications Framework (AQF) level after completing your main course
You are applying for a PhD
You are sponsored by the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade or Defence
You are applying for primary or secondary school study
Your education provider has defaulted and you cannot continue your course
Some moves between school, non-AQF and AQF courses (the factsheet lists these)

body: New Student visa applicants can no longer include a partner or dependent children in their application unless an exemption applies. Exemptions include PhD students, students sponsored by DFAT or Defence, students on a foreign government scholarship, and eligible students from Pacific or ASEAN countries.

Current Student visa holders can no longer add family members after their visa is granted. The department says there are no exemptions to this rule. Family members already included on a current Student visa may be included in the next application if it is made in Australia.
The primary applicant and all family members in an application must be in the same location when it is lodged.

body.note: This is general information, not migration advice. The Department of Home Affairs lists the affected visa types on its Subclass 500 Student visa page. For advice about your situation, speak to a registered migration agent or lawyer.

body: Victorians go to the polls on Saturday 28 November for the 2026 state election. Voting centres will be open from 8am to 6pm, and you can vote at any voting centre in Victoria, according to the Victorian Electoral Commission (VEC).
Voting is compulsory for everyone on the electoral roll. The roll closed at 8pm on Tuesday 3 November, so if you are not sure whether you are enrolled, check your details on the VEC website.

dl: Early voting and telephone-assisted voting open

body: Early voting runs from Wednesday 18 to Friday 27 November, 9am to 6pm each day except Sunday 22 November. You do not need a reason to vote early. The VEC says early voting locations will be published closer to the date.
If you cannot get to a voting centre, you can apply for a postal vote until 6pm on Wednesday 25 November. Ballot packs are posted after nominations close and candidates are confirmed.
Telephone-assisted voting is available for people who are blind, have low vision or have a motor impairment. Registration opens on Wednesday 18 November.

The VEC publishes voting information in other languages on its website, and early and election-day voting centres have how-to-vote information in other languages. You can also call the VEC on 131 832.

मतदाता सूची में दर्ज हर व्यक्ति के लिए मतदान अनिवार्य है। मतदाता सूची मंगलवार, 3 नवंबर को रात 8 बजे बंद हो चुकी है। अगर आपको पक्का नहीं पता कि आपका नाम दर्ज है, तो VEC की वेबसाइट पर अपनी जानकारी जाँच लें।

body: अग्रिम मतदान बुधवार 18 नवंबर से शुक्रवार 27 नवंबर तक रोज़ सुबह 9 बजे से शाम 6 बजे तक होगा, केवल रविवार 22 नवंबर को छोड़कर। पहले वोट देने के लिए कोई कारण बताने की ज़रूरत नहीं है। VEC के अनुसार अग्रिम मतदान केंद्रों की जगहें तारीख़ के क़रीब बताई जाएँगी।
अगर आप मतदान केंद्र तक नहीं जा सकते, तो बुधवार 25 नवंबर शाम 6 बजे तक डाक मत के लिए आवेदन कर सकते हैं। नामांकन बंद होने और उम्मीदवार तय होने के बाद मतपत्र डाक से भेजे जाते हैं।
जो लोग देख नहीं सकते, कम देख पाते हैं या जिन्हें हाथ-पैर चलाने में कठिनाई है, वे टेलीफ़ोन की सहायता से वोट दे सकते हैं। इसका पंजीकरण बुधवार 18 नवंबर से शुरू होगा।
VEC अपनी वेबसाइट पर दूसरी भाषाओं में मतदान की जानकारी देता है, और अग्रिम व चुनाव-दिवस के मतदान केंद्रों पर भी दूसरी भाषाओं में वोट डालने की जानकारी मिलती है। आप VEC को 131 832 पर फ़ोन भी कर सकते हैं।

body: ਵਿਕਟੋਰੀਆ ਦੇ ਵੋਟਰ 2026 ਦੀਆਂ ਸੂਬਾਈ ਚੋਣਾਂ ਲਈ ਸ਼ਨੀਵਾਰ, 28 ਨਵੰਬਰ ਨੂੰ ਵੋਟਾਂ ਪਾਉਣਗੇ। ਵਿਕਟੋਰੀਅਨ ਇਲੈਕਟੋਰਲ ਕਮਿਸ਼ਨ (VEC) ਮੁਤਾਬਕ ਵੋਟਿੰਗ ਕੇਂਦਰ ਸਵੇਰੇ 8 ਵਜੇ ਤੋਂ ਸ਼ਾਮ 6 ਵਜੇ ਤੱਕ ਖੁੱਲ੍ਹੇ ਰਹਿਣਗੇ, ਅਤੇ ਤੁਸੀਂ ਵਿਕਟੋਰੀਆ ਦੇ ਕਿਸੇ ਵੀ ਵੋਟਿੰਗ ਕੇਂਦਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਵੋਟ ਪਾ ਸਕਦੇ ਹੋ।

ਵੋਟਰ ਸੂਚੀ ਵਿੱਚ ਦਰਜ ਹਰ ਵਿਅਕਤੀ ਲਈ ਵੋਟ ਪਾਉਣੀ ਲਾਜ਼ਮੀ ਹੈ। ਵੋਟਰ ਸੂਚੀ ਮੰਗਲਵਾਰ, 3 ਨਵੰਬਰ ਨੂੰ ਰਾਤ 8 ਵਜੇ ਬੰਦ ਹੋ ਚੁੱਕੀ ਹੈ। ਜੇ ਤੁਹਾਨੂੰ ਪੱਕਾ ਨਹੀਂ ਪਤਾ ਕਿ ਤੁਹਾਡਾ ਨਾਂ ਦਰਜ ਹੈ ਜਾਂ ਨਹੀਂ, ਤਾਂ VEC ਦੀ ਵੈੱਬਸਾਈਟ 'ਤੇ ਆਪਣੇ ਵੇਰਵੇ ਜਾਂਚ ਲਓ।

body: ਅਗਾਊਂ ਵੋਟਿੰਗ ਬੁੱਧਵਾਰ 18 ਨਵੰਬਰ ਤੋਂ ਸ਼ੁੱਕਰਵਾਰ 27 ਨਵੰਬਰ ਤੱਕ ਹਰ ਰੋਜ਼ ਸਵੇਰੇ 9 ਵਜੇ ਤੋਂ ਸ਼ਾਮ 6 ਵਜੇ ਤੱਕ ਹੋਵੇਗੀ, ਸਿਰਫ਼ ਐਤਵਾਰ 22 ਨਵੰਬਰ ਨੂੰ ਛੱਡ ਕੇ। ਪਹਿਲਾਂ ਵੋਟ ਪਾਉਣ ਲਈ ਕੋਈ ਕਾਰਨ ਦੱਸਣ ਦੀ ਲੋੜ ਨਹੀਂ। VEC ਮੁਤਾਬਕ ਅਗਾਊਂ ਵੋਟਿੰਗ ਕੇਂਦਰਾਂ ਦੀਆਂ ਥਾਵਾਂ ਤਰੀਕ ਦੇ ਨੇੜੇ ਦੱਸੀਆਂ ਜਾਣਗੀਆਂ।
ਜੇ ਤੁਸੀਂ ਵੋਟਿੰਗ ਕੇਂਦਰ ਨਹੀਂ ਜਾ ਸਕਦੇ, ਤਾਂ ਬੁੱਧਵਾਰ 25 ਨਵੰਬਰ ਸ਼ਾਮ 6 ਵਜੇ ਤੱਕ ਡਾਕ ਵੋਟ ਲਈ ਅਰਜ਼ੀ ਦੇ ਸਕਦੇ ਹੋ। ਨਾਮਜ਼ਦਗੀਆਂ ਬੰਦ ਹੋਣ ਅਤੇ ਉਮੀਦਵਾਰ ਪੱਕੇ ਹੋਣ ਤੋਂ ਬਾਅਦ ਬੈਲਟ ਪੇਪਰ ਡਾਕ ਰਾਹੀਂ ਭੇਜੇ ਜਾਂਦੇ ਹਨ।
ਜਿਹੜੇ ਲੋਕ ਦੇਖ ਨਹੀਂ ਸਕਦੇ, ਘੱਟ ਦੇਖਦੇ ਹਨ ਜਾਂ ਜਿਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਹੱਥਾਂ-ਪੈਰਾਂ ਦੀ ਹਿਲਜੁਲ ਵਿੱਚ ਦਿੱਕਤ ਹੈ, ਉਹ ਫ਼ੋਨ ਦੀ ਸਹਾਇਤਾ ਨਾਲ ਵੋਟ ਪਾ ਸਕਦੇ ਹਨ। ਇਸ ਲਈ ਰਜਿਸਟ੍ਰੇਸ਼ਨ ਬੁੱਧਵਾਰ 18 ਨਵੰਬਰ ਤੋਂ ਸ਼ੁਰੂ ਹੋਵੇਗੀ।

VEC ਆਪਣੀ ਵੈੱਬਸਾਈਟ 'ਤੇ ਹੋਰ ਬੋਲੀਆਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਵੋਟਿੰਗ ਦੀ ਜਾਣਕਾਰੀ ਦਿੰਦਾ ਹੈ, ਅਤੇ ਅਗਾਊਂ ਅਤੇ ਚੋਣਾਂ ਵਾਲੇ ਦਿਨ ਦੇ ਵੋਟਿੰਗ ਕੇਂਦਰਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਵੀ ਹੋਰ ਬੋਲੀਆਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਵੋਟ ਪਾਉਣ ਦੀ ਜਾਣਕਾਰੀ ਮਿਲਦੀ ਹੈ। ਤੁਸੀਂ VEC ਨੂੰ 131 832 'ਤੇ ਫ਼ੋਨ ਵੀ ਕਰ ਸਕਦੇ ਹੋ।

body: The Melbourne Indian is a new, independent news service for Melbourne's Indian communities, and for anyone who wants to know what is happening in them.
We focus on life here: council and state decisions, local business, festivals and faith, and the practical information families need. News from India appears when it affects people in Melbourne.
Every story is free to read. We publish in English, Hindi and Punjabi, and we translate stories where a language edition will be useful to readers.

We report from published records and official sources, and we link to them at the end of every story so you can check our work. We use AI tools to help research, draft and translate. Every story is checked against its sources and approved by an editor before it is published. Sensitive stories, including politics, crime, courts and allegations about people, get extra review.
We do not invent quotes, interviews or photographs. When we get something wrong, we correct it and say so.
We are funded by advertising from local businesses. Advertising and sponsored content are always labelled, and they never decide what we report.

We are just getting started. If you run a community organisation, temple, gurdwara or business and want us to know what you are doing, we would like to hear from you. Email our editors at news@themelbourneindian.com.au. For advertising, email ads@themelbourneindian.com.au.

body: द मेलबर्न इंडियन एक नई, स्वतंत्र समाचार सेवा है, मेलबर्न के भारतीय समुदायों के लिए और उन सभी के लिए जो जानना चाहते हैं कि इन समुदायों में क्या हो रहा है।

हमारा ध्यान यहाँ की ज़िंदगी पर है: काउंसिल और राज्य सरकार के फ़ैसले, स्थानीय व्यवसाय, त्योहार और आस्था, और परिवारों के काम की व्यावहारिक जानकारी। भारत की ख़बरें तब छपेंगी जब उनका असर मेलबर्न में रहने वालों पर पड़ता हो।
हर ख़बर पढ़ने के लिए निःशुल्क है। हम अंग्रेज़ी, हिंदी और पंजाबी में प्रकाशित करते हैं, और जहाँ किसी भाषा में ख़बर पाठकों के काम आए, वहाँ उसका अनुवाद करते हैं।

हम प्रकाशित रिकॉर्ड और आधिकारिक स्रोतों से रिपोर्ट करते हैं, और हर ख़बर के अंत में उनके लिंक देते हैं ताकि आप ख़ुद जाँच सकें। शोध, लेखन और अनुवाद में हम AI टूल्स की मदद लेते हैं। हर ख़बर स्रोतों से मिलाई जाती है और प्रकाशन से पहले एक संपादक उसे मंज़ूरी देता है। राजनीति, अपराध, अदालत और लोगों पर लगे आरोपों जैसी संवेदनशील ख़बरों की अतिरिक्त जाँच होती है।
हम कोई उद्धरण, साक्षात्कार या तस्वीर गढ़ते नहीं हैं। ग़लती होने पर हम उसे सुधारते हैं और यह साफ़ बताते हैं।
हमारा ख़र्च स्थानीय व्यवसायों के विज्ञापनों से चलता है। विज्ञापन और प्रायोजित सामग्री पर हमेशा स्पष्ट लेबल होता है, और वे यह तय नहीं करते कि हम क्या रिपोर्ट करें।

हम अभी शुरुआत कर रहे हैं। अगर आप कोई सामुदायिक संस्था, मंदिर, गुरुद्वारा या व्यवसाय चलाते हैं और चाहते हैं कि हमें आपके काम की जानकारी हो, तो हम आपसे सुनना चाहेंगे। हमारे संपादकों को news@themelbourneindian.com.au पर ईमेल करें। विज्ञापन के लिए ads@themelbourneindian.com.au पर ईमेल करें।

body: ਦ ਮੈਲਬਰਨ ਇੰਡੀਅਨ ਇੱਕ ਨਵੀਂ, ਆਜ਼ਾਦ ਖ਼ਬਰ ਸੇਵਾ ਹੈ, ਮੈਲਬਰਨ ਦੇ ਭਾਰਤੀ ਭਾਈਚਾਰਿਆਂ ਲਈ ਅਤੇ ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਸਾਰਿਆਂ ਲਈ ਜੋ ਜਾਣਨਾ ਚਾਹੁੰਦੇ ਹਨ ਕਿ ਇਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਭਾਈਚਾਰਿਆਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਕੀ ਹੋ ਰਿਹਾ ਹੈ।

ਸਾਡਾ ਧਿਆਨ ਇੱਥੋਂ ਦੀ ਜ਼ਿੰਦਗੀ 'ਤੇ ਹੈ: ਕੌਂਸਲ ਅਤੇ ਸੂਬਾ ਸਰਕਾਰ ਦੇ ਫ਼ੈਸਲੇ, ਸਥਾਨਕ ਕਾਰੋਬਾਰ, ਤਿਉਹਾਰ ਅਤੇ ਆਸਥਾ, ਅਤੇ ਪਰਿਵਾਰਾਂ ਦੇ ਕੰਮ ਆਉਣ ਵਾਲੀ ਜਾਣਕਾਰੀ। ਭਾਰਤ ਦੀਆਂ ਖ਼ਬਰਾਂ ਉਦੋਂ ਛਪਣਗੀਆਂ ਜਦੋਂ ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਦਾ ਅਸਰ ਮੈਲਬਰਨ ਵਿੱਚ ਰਹਿਣ ਵਾਲਿਆਂ 'ਤੇ ਪੈਂਦਾ ਹੋਵੇ।
ਹਰ ਖ਼ਬਰ ਪੜ੍ਹਨ ਲਈ ਮੁਫ਼ਤ ਹੈ। ਅਸੀਂ ਅੰਗਰੇਜ਼ੀ, ਹਿੰਦੀ ਅਤੇ ਪੰਜਾਬੀ ਵਿੱਚ ਛਾਪਦੇ ਹਾਂ, ਅਤੇ ਜਿੱਥੇ ਕਿਸੇ ਬੋਲੀ ਵਿੱਚ ਖ਼ਬਰ ਪਾਠਕਾਂ ਦੇ ਕੰਮ ਆਵੇ, ਉੱਥੇ ਉਸਦਾ ਅਨੁਵਾਦ ਕਰਦੇ ਹਾਂ।

ਅਸੀਂ ਛਪੇ ਹੋਏ ਰਿਕਾਰਡਾਂ ਅਤੇ ਸਰਕਾਰੀ ਸਰੋਤਾਂ ਤੋਂ ਰਿਪੋਰਟ ਕਰਦੇ ਹਾਂ, ਅਤੇ ਹਰ ਖ਼ਬਰ ਦੇ ਅਖ਼ੀਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਦੇ ਲਿੰਕ ਦਿੰਦੇ ਹਾਂ ਤਾਂ ਜੋ ਤੁਸੀਂ ਆਪ ਜਾਂਚ ਕਰ ਸਕੋ। ਖੋਜ, ਲਿਖਾਈ ਅਤੇ ਅਨੁਵਾਦ ਵਿੱਚ ਅਸੀਂ AI ਟੂਲਾਂ ਦੀ ਮਦਦ ਲੈਂਦੇ ਹਾਂ। ਹਰ ਖ਼ਬਰ ਸਰੋਤਾਂ ਨਾਲ ਮਿਲਾਈ ਜਾਂਦੀ ਹੈ ਅਤੇ ਛਪਣ ਤੋਂ ਪਹਿਲਾਂ ਕੋਈ ਸੰਪਾਦਕ ਉਸਨੂੰ ਮਨਜ਼ੂਰੀ ਦਿੰਦਾ ਹੈ। ਸਿਆਸਤ, ਜੁਰਮ, ਅਦਾਲਤਾਂ ਅਤੇ ਲੋਕਾਂ 'ਤੇ ਲੱਗੇ ਦੋਸ਼ਾਂ ਵਰਗੀਆਂ ਸੰਵੇਦਨਸ਼ੀਲ ਖ਼ਬਰਾਂ ਦੀ ਵਾਧੂ ਜਾਂਚ ਹੁੰਦੀ ਹੈ।
ਅਸੀਂ ਕੋਈ ਹਵਾਲਾ, ਇੰਟਰਵਿਊ ਜਾਂ ਤਸਵੀਰ ਨਹੀਂ ਘੜਦੇ। ਗ਼ਲਤੀ ਹੋਣ 'ਤੇ ਅਸੀਂ ਉਸਨੂੰ ਸੁਧਾਰਦੇ ਹਾਂ ਅਤੇ ਸਾਫ਼ ਦੱਸਦੇ ਹਾਂ।

body: The royal commission into corruption on Victoria's major infrastructure projects began its first public hearings in Collingwood on Monday 9 November, less than three weeks before the state election.

Opening the hearings, counsel assisting Chris Young KC said the commission had requested more than 110,000 documents, sent hundreds of notices and already questioned witnesses in private hearings, according to ABC News coverage of the hearing.

The first hearings are examining the Gap Road level crossing removal in Sunbury, part of the Sunbury line upgrade. They focus on a two-day work stoppage on 6 and 7 June 2022, during a shutdown of the line for critical works. Mr Young outlined allegations that work resumed after a meeting at the CFMEU's offices on 7 June, on terms that handed control of the site to the union. He said the commission would examine what happened, what arrangements were made, what they cost and what the government knew.

body.note: Allegations aired at a royal commission are not proven. Mr Young said some of them have been denied. The commission has made no findings.

body.h: What the commission heard on day one

body: The hearing was read a 2017 memo by contractor John Holland which said the CFMEU had "unprecedented access to ministers" and was a key industrial organisation in the premier's faction at the time, ABC News reported. The memo also said the union would probably know about government tenders before they were announced. These are claims recorded in a document, not findings.

Notes from a contractors' meeting recorded a threat that workers would be "smashed" if they turned up, Mr Young told the hearing. Police and WorkSafe Victoria were notified, the commission heard, but police treated it as a workplace safety matter and took no action.

The June 2022 shutdown at Gap Road pushed the project's costs up by an estimated $6 million, the commission heard. Mr Young said other contractors had described "remarkably similar" experiences on other major projects.
Premier Ben Carroll denied knowing about the CFMEU's access to senior officials and ministers. "What today's hearings show is that I am a premier that will make the tough decisions," he said.

body.h: What the commission will look at

body: Mr Young set out themes the inquiry expects to explore. They include allegations that the union placed unelected delegates on sites as health and safety representatives, sometimes through labour-hire companies, and that contractors were often left to deal with disruption themselves by "buying peace" and pricing its cost into their bids. He said those costs were shared with the state or passed on to it.

He tendered a June 2023 briefing to Jacinta Allan, then the transport infrastructure minister, which raised concerns including pressure on contractors, excess staffing on sites, a rise in full-time union delegates and threats of unprotected industrial action. The briefing records concerns raised at the time and is not a finding. AAP has reported that Ms Allan, who later became premier, will be required to give evidence, but it is not yet known when.
Later hearing blocks will examine alleged links between organised crime and the construction industry, and how government money was allocated and projects chosen.
Mr Young also warned that threatening or punishing a witness is a serious offence, and said any reported threat would be referred to Victoria Police.

The Royal Commission into the Integrity of Major Public and Civil Infrastructure Construction Projects in Victoria was established on 20 August 2026. It is led by the Honourable Christopher Kourakis AC, a former chief justice of South Australia, and its final report is due by 20 August 2027.

Premier Ben Carroll called the inquiry as his first act after replacing Ms Allan, who had resisted calls from across the parliament for a royal commission. The calls followed reporting by Nine newspapers in 2024 alleging corruption and criminal infiltration of the CFMEU and Big Build sites. Parts of the union were placed into administration by the federal government in August 2024.

A report for the union's administrators by barrister Geoffrey Watson SC estimated that alleged corrupt conduct had effectively cost Victorian taxpayers $15 billion. That figure is Mr Watson's estimate, and testing claims like it is part of the commission's work.

This block of hearings runs until Friday 20 November, overlapping with early voting, which opens on Wednesday 18 November. Polling day is Saturday 28 November. A second block of hearings is expected before the end of the year, ABC News has reported.
ABC News has reported that the hearings will run through about two weeks of the four-week campaign. Mr Carroll has said that "integrity is not negotiable".

body: A Hindu temple in Melbourne's west was left without power on the eve of Diwali after its electricity was cut for the second time in eight days, according to MPs from both major parties. The incidents were first reported by The Indian Sun and South Asia Times.

Evan Mulholland, the Opposition's spokesman for multicultural and multifaith affairs, said power to the SMVS Swaminarayan temple in Mount Cottrell, next to Tarneit, was cut on Saturday 31 October, and the community paid thousands of dollars to have it reconnected. He said vandals returned on Saturday 7 November, the night before Diwali, and cut the power again at the main electrical board. The temple could not restore it in time for its celebrations, he said.
"No faith community in Victoria should have to live like this," Mr Mulholland said in a statement on Sunday, The Indian Sun reported.

body.note: The details of the power cuts come from MPs' statements. The Melbourne Indian has not been able to confirm them with Victoria Police, which had not commented publicly at the time of publication. No one has been charged and the motive is not known.

body: Tarneit's Labor MP, Dylan Wight, visited the temple on Sunday. He told The Indian Sun he was "deeply disappointed and concerned by the latest act of vandalism", and that no community should have to keep repairing damage to its place of worship.

Mr Wight also told the paper that Labor would provide $200,000 for security upgrades at the temple if it is re-elected on 28 November, with the work to be decided with temple management. How the money would be paid and when work could start have not been announced.

The Liberal candidate for Tarneit, Venkat Ram Upparlapalle, visited the temple last week and called for a thorough police investigation, stronger security and accountability. "A temple should be a place of peace, prayer and belonging," he wrote on social media.

Earlier this month Premier Ben Carroll announced an $11 million Temple and Gurdwara Safety Fund, for security and other upgrades at Hindu temples and Sikh gurdwaras, at the Sri Durga Temple in Deanside. South Asia Times reported that the Deanside temple would receive $1 million. The Melbourne Indian could not find a Coalition funding commitment for the SMVS temple at the time of publication.

Mr Mulholland said the temple had faced theft, break-ins, a firebombing, a vehicle being driven into the building and repeated interference with its power over more than a decade, sometimes before major festivals, The Indian Sun reported.

After a break-in before Holi in March 2025, temple trustee Biren Joshi told The Australia Today it was the eighth incident in eight years, and that no arrests had been made for any of them. The temple has received government money for security before: The Indian Sun reported that funding for fencing, gates and CCTV was set aside for it under the federal Safer Communities Fund in 2020.
Anyone with information can contact Crime Stoppers on 1800 333 000 or at crimestoppersvic.com.au, and can stay anonymous. In an emergency, call triple zero (000).
en.dek: The SMVS Swaminarayan temple near Tarneit lost power twice in eight days, according to MPs from both major parties. Labor has pledged $200,000 for its security if re-elected.

body: Judges would have to treat an attack on someone who steps in to help another person as an aggravating factor when sentencing, under a law the Victorian Coalition says it will introduce if it wins the state election on 28 November.

Opposition Leader Jess Wilson has named the proposal Aidan's Law, after Aidan Becker, a 22-year-old off-duty security guard who died after he was stabbed at Mernda railway station, in Melbourne's north, in March while trying to help a 14-year-old boy. Ms Wilson said the policy followed a request from Mr Becker's mother, Natalie, AAP reported.
"If you're brave enough to stand up for someone else, the law should stand up for you," Ms Wilson said.

Victorian courts can already take that kind of circumstance into account, but the law does not specifically require them to, according to AAP. Details such as wording, penalties and timing were not part of the announcement as reported.

body.note: Several people have been charged in connection with Mr Becker's death. The case is before the courts.

body.h: Labor's pitch on the same day

body: Premier Ben Carroll promised 200 more police reservists, former officers who would answer phones and staff counters at police stations, on top of 400 already being recruited. He also announced two new police stations and the rebuilding or upgrading of four others, AAP reported.
"Victorians have been very clear that they want to see someone at the counter when they walk into their local station," Mr Carroll said.
The Labor government has started a review of Victoria's sentencing laws, with public consultation due to begin in April 2027.
Early voting opens on Wednesday 18 November, and election day is Saturday 28 November.
en.dek: Jess Wilson says courts would have to treat an attack on a Good Samaritan as more serious if the Coalition wins on 28 November. Labor is promising 200 more police reservists.

pages.standards:
How we decide what to publish, how we check it, and how we fix mistakes.

What we cover

We cover news that matters to people of Indian heritage living in Melbourne: local and state government, business, festivals and faith, education, health services and community life. News from India appears when it affects readers here.

Sources

We report from published records, official announcements, organisers' own listings and documents we can link to. Every story ends with its sources and the date we checked them. When sources disagree, we say so or we hold the story.

How a story gets published

We sort every story into one of three levels before it goes anywhere.

Routine
Official dates, public event details, program facts and notices taken directly from an official or organiser's source. These are checked against that source before publication.
Review
Election promises, policy debates, business disputes and anything a reasonable person could contest. A person approves these before publication.
Sensitive
Crime, courts, allegations about people, public safety, health, migration or legal advice, and anything involving children. These get careful human editorial review, and legal advice where needed.

When we are unsure which level applies, we treat the story as the higher one.

AI tools

We use AI tools to help find sources, draft stories and translate them into Hindi and Punjabi. We do not use AI to invent quotes, people, interviews or images of real events. Translations are checked against the English original, and we welcome corrections from readers fluent in each language.

Politics

We do not endorse candidates or parties. In election coverage we give the same treatment to every candidate and stick to what they have said and done.

Advertising

Advertisers do not influence our reporting. Advertising and sponsored content are always clearly labelled as such.

Corrections

When we get something wrong, we fix it and add a note at the end of the story saying what changed and when. To report an error, email news@themelbourneindian.com.au.
